question.prompt: There are exactly \(K\) positive integers \(b\) with \(5 \le b \le 2024\) such that the base-\(b\) integer \(2024_b\) is divisible by \(16\) (where \(16\) is in base ten). What is the sum of the digits of \(K?\)

solutions.title: Factor and check remainders
solutions.explanation:
The useful observation is that expanding the base-\(b\) number produces an expression with a factor of \(2\):
\[
2024_b=2b^3+2b+4=2(b+1)(b^2-b+2).
\]
Thus \(2024_b\) is divisible by \(16\) exactly when \((b+1)(b^2-b+2)\) is divisible by \(8\).

This product's remainder modulo \(8\) depends only on the remainder of \(b\). Checking all eight possibilities gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrr}
b\pmod 8&0&1&2&3&4&5&6&7\\ \hline
(b+1)(b^2-b+2)\pmod 8&2&4&4&0&6&4&0&0
\end{array}
\]
For example, when \(b\equiv3\pmod8\), the product is congruent to \(4(9-3+2)=32\equiv0\pmod8\). Therefore the qualifying bases are exactly those congruent to \(3,6,\) or \(7\) modulo \(8\).

Since \(2024=253\cdot8\), each of these three residue classes occurs \(253\) times among \(1,2,\ldots,2024\). Of the numbers below \(5\), only \(3\) was counted, so
\[
K=3\cdot253-1=758.
\]
The requested digit sum is \(7+5+8=\boxed{20}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
